jobs.occupation: Research Manager AI & Data, Simulation and Quantum (m/f/d),Ingolstadt,Wolfsburg,Stuttgart,München (Forschungsreferent/in)
jobs.description: What if your next project shaped the next decade of innovation?  At TWT Science & Innovation, we're looking for a Research Manager who leads collaborative, international research at the intersection of AI, Data, Simulation, Processes, and Quantum Computing - turning scientific excellence into technological breakthroughs. Over the last decade, 22 researchers from TWT became university professors. Now, we're searching for the next mind to push the frontier forward.  About the Role As a Research Manager, you'll lead interdisciplinary R&D programs with top universities such as MIT, Harvard, Berkeley, Stanford and ETH Zurich - advancing foundational research in Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Simulation, Processes, and Quantum Computing. You will drive both collaborative research consortia and your own independent research programs, and you will work closely with international funding bodies, scientific partners, and innovation networks. The results, insights, and technologies you develop will be transferred into industry sectors such as Engineering, Automotive, Aerospace, Energy, Climate & Sustainability, and Health. What You'll Do Lead and manage international research programs across AI, Data Science, Simulation, Processes, and Quantum Computing. Build and run multi-partner research consortia with world-leading universities, tech networks, and public funding agencies. What You Bring PhD or Postdoctoral degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or related fields preferably from a top university.  Proven success in coordinating international and interdisciplinary research programs.  Strong expertise in AI, data-driven engineering, simulation-based design, or computational processes. Experience with EU or national funding programs (Horizon Europe, DFG, BMBF, etc.).  Fluent in English and German; strong communicator across cultures and disciplines.  A growth mindset, and a passion for scientific impact. Why Join TWT? Shape the technologies that will define the next decade. Work in an environment where scientific excellence meets innovation. A place where research careers grow into scientific legacies We're not just hiring a Research Manager - we're inviting a mind that dares to imagine more. jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support the Spectrum & Regulatory Affairs team, Airbus Defence and Space is looking for a

Working Student within Frequency Management (d/f/m)

You are a full time student, looking for a working student position and want to get to know the work of Airbus?  Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Frequency Management team as a working student (d/f/m) with approx. 18 hours a week!

- Location: Taufkirchen/Munich
- Start: As soon as possible
- Duration: 12 months

Definition working student

Working students are students who are enrolled at a University or some other institution of higher education, and who are employed in a reasonably long, fixed-term position parallel to their studies. This position must not be confused with an internship or with the possibility of writing a final thesis.

This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. A working student's main focus remains on their studies, which is why, during term-time, working students are not allowed to work more than 20 hours per week.

Working students therefore usually work near their place of study, so as to conveniently combine studying and employment.

Your location

Our site is just a stone's throw away from Munich, the beautiful capital of Bavaria. Are you into sports and other outdoor activities? The Alps and Lake Starnberg are within an hour’s reach, offering a multitude of recreational options.

Your benefits

- Attractive salary and work-life balance with an 18-hour week (flexitime).
- A final thesis is possible after consultation with the department.
- Mobile working after agreement with the department.
- Traveling overseas or within Germany (team events) is possible after consultation and agreement from the department.
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Supporting interference simulations between different RF systems in MATLAB
- Develop software modules such as propagation models, antenna radiation patterns for incorporation into the RF simulation. Including the development of relevant documentation.
- Support the development of technical reports for various international fora such as the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a specialized agency of the United Nations.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Enrolled student in Electrical Engineering, General Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering or a similar field of study
- Basic knowledge of wireless communications, especially in calculating Link Budgets
- Advanced Programming skills, preferably with MATLAB
- English: Fluent
- German or French would be a plus
- You are a good team player, have excellent communication skills, and are able to work autonomously and proactively.

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrolment certificate.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth

By submitting your CV or application you are consenting to Airbus using and storing information about you for monitoring purposes relating to your application or future employment. This information will only be used by Airbus.
Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

At Airbus, we support you to work, connect and collaborate more easily and flexibly. Wherever possible, we foster flexible working arrangements to stimulate innovative thinking.

html Senior Industrialization Engineer – Space Manufacturing (all genders)Garching, Taufkirchen / Full-time / Permanent employee About us

Blackwave designs, manufactures and ships flight-qualified, commercial off-the-shelf composite overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs) for launch vehicles and satellites. Founded in 2016 and headquartered in Munich, Germany, the company delivers COPVs from a standardized portfolio with flight heritage. The approach reduces lead time from months to days while ensuring that each tank is qualified and flight-ready. Blackwave's mission is to end COPV failure in spaceflight. The company employs more than 150 people across manufacturing facilities in Germany and Texas.

More information at Blackwave.com and the procurement platform COPV.com.

Senior Industrialization Engineer – Space Manufacturing (all genders)
Garching, Taufkirchen / Full-time / Permanent employee YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

THE WHY

To end COPV failure in spaceflight.

Blackwave manufactures carbon structural components for rockets, and satellites – with the ambition to make space access as reliable and scalable as automotive production. That demands a manufacturing operation that grows with us: process-stable, reproducible, and ramp-up-proof. That's where you come in.

THE WHAT

Be the process mastermind of our manufacturing operation.

At Blackwave, you coordinate production engineering across all teams, set priorities on open issues, and drive our manufacturing processes toward serial production standards – scalable, resilient, and ready for every ramp-up.

Drive & Improve Processes

Systematically analyze production processes for scalability and robustness – then actively raise the bar.

Own and maintain a structured, always-current list of open points across all production steps.

Set the Standards

Implement 5S standards at workstations and in material handling – consistently and sustainably.

Push fixture and tooling improvements from concept through manufacturing, implementation, and verification.

Machine Performance

Coordinate stakeholders and engineers when scoping new machines, ensuring performance reliably meets requirements.

YOUR PROFILE

- Space-to-Automotive Mindset: you understand the sensitivity of the space industry and translate it into robust, scalable manufacturing processes
- Lean & CI Methods: proven experience with Kaizen, SMED, 5S, and related tools to improve throughput, reduce waste, and drive continuous improvement
- Risk Management: identify production risks early, develop mitigation plans, and support successful production ramp-ups
- Root Cause Mastery: experienced in structured problem-solving methods such as 5 Whys, Ishikawa, and FMEA, turning production issues into sustainable corrective actions
- Cross-functional Communicator: translate shopfloor realities into clear inputs for Planning, Engineering, QA, and Management while keeping stakeholders aligned
- Shopfloor Driven: enjoy working hands-on with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, and operators to solve problems where they occur
- Thrives in Complexity: comfortable operating in fast-changing environments, balancing immediate production needs with long-term process improvements
- Change Agent: support the introduction of new technologies, equipment, and processes while helping teams adapt and grow
- Languages: Fluent German and English (C1 level) essential
- Location: Regular on-site presence required across our Garching and Taufkirchen locations

WHAT WE OFFER

- Ownership & creative freedom – you actively shape how we bring aerospace components to serial production
- Flexible hours & mobile working – work-life balance is a real commitment, not a talking point
- Start-up spirit meets aerospace – flat hierarchies, fast decisions, genuine room for initiative
- Personalized benefits – choose between Germany Ticket, Egym Wellpass, or a tax-free Givve Card
- Fresh food daily – shared lunches with healthy, varied dishes
